title: Checkmate the Sphinx
summary: Let the enemy pawn cage its own king, then coordinate king, knight and bishop before promotion.

nodes.question: What does the pawn on a6 take away from Black’s king?
nodes.explanation: Begin after a6 ...bxa6: White has Kc3, Na2, Bb2 and a3 against Ka4, a6 and h3. The earlier eight-piece pawn offer remains source context outside this exact checked tree.

branches.title: Mate after the king goes to a5
commentary: Begin from the complete seven-piece diagram after ...bxa6. The black pawn on a6 will obstruct its king.
Kc2 frees c3 for the knight and controls b3, denying the king’s escape toward the center.
Be5 both attacks h2 along the diagonal and prepares the mating net near a5/a3.
h1=Q promotes, but the new queen has no tempo before White’s checking finish.
Nc3+ checks Ka4 while keeping the king confined near its own a6 pawn.
Ka5 chooses the upper escape square.
Bc7# mates along c7–a5. The a6 pawn blocks its own king, while the knight and White’s king cover the remaining exits.
branches.explanation: Bc7# mates along c7–a5. The a6 pawn blocks its own king, while the knight and White’s king cover the remaining exits.

branches.title: Mate after the king goes to a3
commentary: Compare the source’s lower king escape from the same knight check.
Kc2 makes room for Nc3 and controls b3.
h1=Q creates a queen without stopping the checking attack.
Nc3+ forces the king to answer the knight.
Kxa3 takes White’s a3 pawn, but enters the second mating diagonal.
Bd6# mates along d6–a3. Kc2 and Nc3 close the remaining escape squares, despite Black’s new queen.
branches.explanation: Bd6# mates along d6–a3. Kc2 and Nc3 close the remaining escape squares, despite Black’s new queen.

exercises.prompt: Why does Kc2 matter before the knight check?
exercises.answer: It frees c3 for the knight and holds b3. Be5 can then prepare either Bc7 mate or Bd6 mate after Black promotes.
